name: PT Argo Pantes Tbk

frontmatter.title: Argo Pantes: a warehouse landlord priced as if the old mill site were already a township
frontmatter.summary: ARGO has become a Greater Jakarta warehouse landlord, but the equity is priced at several times what the land and the rent book are worth. Rents sit below market, dollar debt turns operating profit into losses, and a related party is the largest tenant. We initiate at SELL with a target of Rp338.
thesis: The business is a warehouse lessor now, not a textile maker: rent, energy recharge and a cooperation line are almost all of revenue and the textile line is a rounding error [S15].

The asset is the land: two titled industrial sites in Tangerang and Cibitung, most of which is neither built nor let. We mark each site against its own municipality's land average, cut by the property card's land-bank haircut, and the shares still price the undeveloped balance well above the haircut mark we are willing to underwrite for it [S15][S20].

Earnings do not reach the equity: a foreign-exchange loss of IDR46.5bn in nine months of 2026 swallowed an operating profit of about IDR22.6bn on our forecast, and a zero-coupon dollar bond keeps that exposure alive [S15].

The signed build-to-suit programme is real and improves cash flow, but it is a capex programme that must be debt-funded against an equity base of IDR157.1bn and an accumulated deficit the company cannot dividend out of [S7][S15].

At Rp1,145 the market pays more for the undeveloped land than the Tangerang municipal average supports after the land-bank haircut, before any discount to appraised assets. That is the bull case, not the base case [S20].
Structural flags compound the gap: insiders hold 92.4%, the free float is 6.2%, and the controlling shareholder is shared with Alam Sutera Realty [S0][S3].

catalysts.event: J&T Cargo build-to-suit warehouse completion and rent commencement
FY2026 audited results: how much of the IIF term loan is drawn and on what terms
Maybank dollar working-capital lines mature and must be rolled
Annual public expose: letting progress on the refurbishment programme

blocks.text: **SELL, target Rp338, total return -70.4% against the Rp1,145 price.**

Argo Pantes is a 1977-vintage integrated textile manufacturer that has spent a decade converting its two factory sites into warehouses and letting them to third-party logistics and industrial tenants [S4][S6]. The pivot is genuine and the tenants are real: J&T Cargo signed a ten-year build-to-suit lease worth IDR221.0bn in February 2026, and United Chemicals, part of the Omya group, signed a sixty-four-month lease worth IDR48.1bn in July 2026 covering office and loading areas [S6]. Rent and the energy recharge that comes with it are now almost all of revenue [S15].

The problem is the price. ARGO owns 443,000 sqm in Cikokol, Tangerang and 199,560 sqm inside the industrial estate at Cibitung in Bekasi, of which 215,535 sqm of the Tangerang land is held on HGB title extended to 2057 [S10][S11][S15]. Only 170,283 sqm was leased at end-2025 [S4]. We value the undeveloped balance at each site's own municipal land average less the land-bank haircut the property card requires, and the standing estate at a warehouse cap rate [S15][S20]. That produces an RNAV leg of Rp429 per share after the 40.0% discount at the floor of the house band, and a target of Rp338 after the engine's further 20.0% float discount, so the total haircut to appraised NAV is inside the band rather than below it. The market is not valuing an industrial warehouse estate; it is paying more for the undeveloped land than the Tangerang and Bekasi comparables support once the card's haircut is applied [S20].

Three things move the value. First, **land**. We mark Cikokol and Cibitung separately, each against its own municipal average less the card's haircut [S20]; the bull case raises that mark by the same proportion the bear cuts it, and even the bull stays below the municipal averages. Second, **the rent book**. Rent revenue of IDR61.5bn in nine months of 2026 on 170,283 sqm of leased space is concentrated: the largest tenant is a related party at 22.7% of revenue, and its revenue fell by a third year on year [S15]. There is no warehouse rent benchmark in our record - the JLL data carries occupancy and asking-rent growth, not a rent per square metre - so we do not claim the book is under-let [S18]. Third, **the dollar**. Nine months of 2026 produced a IDR46.5bn foreign-exchange loss that turned operating profit into a net loss of IDR-36.0bn [S15]; the IDR542.0bn subordinated bond and a dollar working-capital line keep that lever live [S15].

The counter-argument deserves stating plainly. If the Cikokol site were read at the municipality's average land price with no haircut, then ARGO's asset value would be a multiple of ours and today's price would not be absurd [S20]. We do not believe it, because the averages cover land of every use rather than industrial estates, the site is zoned and used as a warehouse estate, no rezoning is disclosed in anything we read, and the company's own strategy is to build more warehouses on it rather than sell it [S12][S15]. But that is the argument that would prove us wrong, and it is the one the red team should attack first.

ARGO is a single legal entity, PT Argo Pantes Tbk, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 1991 and part of the Argo Manunggal group [S2][S4]. It reports two operating segments, textile and rent, and states that no component of the company has separately available financial information [S15]. The company employed 109 people at the last count, which is itself a statement about what the business has become [S0].

The revenue mix has already turned. In the nine months to September 2026 net revenue was IDR78.7bn: rent IDR61.5bn, an energy recharge line billed to tenants, a cooperation agreement line, and a residual textile line that is under one percent of the total [S15]. Management describes the company as focused on logistics and warehousing, serving more than thirty local and international customers, and dates the transformation to 2016, when it began using its Tangerang and Bekasi assets for warehousing [S4][S6]. The segment note still carries the historic textile label because the segment definition has not been redrawn [S15].

The estate is two sites. The Cikokol site on Jalan MH Thamrin in Tangerang is the former integrated mill, with 443,000 sqm of land [S10]. The Cibitung site sits inside the same industrial estate in Bekasi with 199,560 sqm [S11]. Both are in the Greater Jakarta industrial belt, which is where modern warehousing demand is concentrated [S18]. Lettable area was 170,283 sqm at end-2025 against 145,250 sqm a year earlier, and management is refurbishing a further seventy-five thousand sqm across the two sites in 2026 [S4][S12].

The customer book is long-lease, largely single-tenant and concentrated. J&T Cargo's build-to-suit lease runs ten years for a warehouse on land of more than forty-four thousand sqm carrying over twenty-three thousand sqm of building and office space, with main construction starting mid-2026 and completion targeted for February 2027 [S7][S13]. The United Chemicals lease runs sixty-four months to the end of 2031 [S6]. The largest single customer, PT Argo Manunggal Triasta, produced 22.7% of net revenue in nine months of 2026, and that customer is a related party; related-party rent was IDR11.0bn in the same period, identical to the prior year to the rupiah [S15].

The controlling shareholder is PT Argo Manunggal Land Development with 38.7% [S3]. The same holding company is named in Alam Sutera Realty's annual report as one of its controlling shareholders, with The Ning King and family as ultimate beneficial owner, and the two issuers share commissioners [S3]. One commissioner is the second-largest shareholder of PT Seko Fajar Plantation, the independent commissioner is a director there, and another commissioner sits on the Alam Sutera board [S3].

The strategy is straightforward and land-constrained: refurbish the old textile sheds, build to suit for committed logistics tenants, and re-let the space at rising market rents [S12]. There is no development-for-sale business, no township and no residential presales, which is why the usual developer KPIs do not apply and the property method has to be adapted rather than applied off the shelf [S15].

The warehouse business ARGO has moved into is a different economic animal from the textile business it left. A mill earns a manufacturing margin on throughput and is exposed to cotton, polyester and labour. A warehouse landlord earns a rent per square metre per month on a lease that runs for years, funds the building once, and then collects. The landlord's risk moves from the commodity cycle to the tenant's credit and the cost of the debt raised to build the shed. That shift is the reason a property method, rather than a manufacturer's method, is the right lens here.

The relevant market is modern warehouse space in Greater Jakarta, not textiles and not residential property. Occupancy in modern warehouses reached 97% in the third quarter of 2026 out of a supply base of about three million sqm, and asking rents rose four percent in the nine months to September 2026 [S18]. Demand comes from logistics operators, then manufacturing, electronics, retail and fast-moving consumer goods, and investment activity continued through 2026, including a September transaction involving a five-warehouse portfolio with two hundred and thirty thousand sqm of net lettable area [S18].

Two structural forces support the space. E-commerce and third-party logistics have made the Greater Jakarta belt the country's distribution hub, and the build-to-suit format, where a tenant commits to a lease before the shed is built, has become the standard way to add grade-A space without taking speculative vacancy risk [S6][S18]. Rents are rising but not sharply, which is consistent with a market that is tight on occupancy while new supply keeps pricing honest [S18].

Against that market ARGO is a small, sub-scale landlord with an unusual asset. Its competitive position rests on land it already owns in two established locations, acquired decades ago at historic cost, plus the ability to lease to tenants who want a specific building in a specific place [S4][S15]. Its weakness is that most of its stock is old: the sheds were built for a textile operation, ceiling heights and loading configurations are not grade-A, and the company is spending 2026 refurbishing rather than building greenfield [S12]. That is why the rent per square metre is below what the market gets for modern space [S15][S18].

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is low: the land is owned, contractors compete for build-to-suit work, and a Chinese contractor was appointed for the J&T phase [S7]. Buyer power is high and rising, because tenants are large logistics operators who negotiate long leases and can choose between competing estates in Bekasi, Karawang and increasingly Subang [S18]. New entrants are plentiful in grade-A space but constrained exactly where ARGO is strong, in already-developed locations inside the Jakarta belt. Substitutes are limited, since a distribution business needs a shed. Rivalry is moderate, segmented by location and by building quality [S18].

The regulatory setting matters less for warehouses than for residential developers. There is no presales VAT incentive to depend on, no land-bank permitting cycle in the residential sense, and no housing credit policy lever. What matters is HGB tenure, extended to 2057 on 215,535 sqm of the Tangerang land while the remaining Tangerang and Bekasi parcels expire in 2030 [S15], land and building tax, and the cost and currency of debt. The macro deck's rupiah path and the BI rate feed straight into that cost, which is why the balance sheet rather than the letting market is the swing factor in this name [S0].

The land market is the other external influence and it dominates the valuation. The energy minister said in August 2026 that industrial land in Indonesia is priced at up to 2,000,000 rupiah per sqm against a far lower figure in Vietnam, as part of a competitiveness argument about industrial estates [S19]. That is a national "up to" ceiling, not a site comparable, and we no longer use it. The commercial property adviser's survey puts the average Jabodetabek land price at 14,824,953 rupiah per sqm for Tangerang and 10,985,202 rupiah per sqm for Bekasi; those are 2H2025 figures, roughly twelve months stale at this report's date, and they cover land of every use rather than industrial estates [S20]. They are the only municipal land comparables in the record, which is why we use them with a stated haircut rather than substituting a judgement from outside it.

Market share is not the right frame for a company with a market value of a few trillion rupiah and roughly IDR105.8bn of annual revenue [S0]. It is a niche owner-operator of two sites, not a participant in the national warehouse market in any meaningful share sense.

**Revenue.** FY2025 net revenue was IDR112.3bn, up from IDR103.0bn [S4]. The nine months to September 2026 came in at IDR78.7bn, below the annual base, because the cooperation and energy recharge lines fell even as rent rose [S15]. We forecast IDR105.8bn for FY2026E, then IDR127.0bn as the J&T lease starts in February 2027 and the United Chemicals lease runs a full year [S6][S7]. Growth then decelerates as the refurbishment programme converts area: IDR144.7bn in FY2028E, easing toward a long-run rate of 10.0%.

The revenue build needs a warning about the template. ARGO does not sell property, so there is no presales line, no handover lag and no marketing-sales KPI of the kind the property card normally demands [S15]. We hold the presales input at a nominal 0.0% and model the letting book in recurring revenue instead. What a reader should watch is not presales but signed lease value and lettable area, both of which are disclosed release by release [S4][S6].

**Margins and costs.** The LK presents a natural-expense profit and loss with no cost-of-sales line: professional fees, salaries, utilities, land and building tax, depreciation, outsourcing, rental, repairs, insurance, textile cost of goods and agent fees, then a final-tax line and the non-operating items [S15]. That is why the data pack's cost-of-sales line is effectively nil for one year and near nil for the next, and why the gross margin printed in the table above is an artefact of the direct cash-flow method rather than an economics fact [S0]. We rebuild the cost base from the LK's own lines: a property cost ratio of roughly half of revenue for utilities, salaries, tax, repairs, insurance and agent fees, and a corporate and depreciation block of 31.6%, with depreciation itself at IDR9.2bn for nine months [S15]. EBITDA margin lands near a third: 33.0% against 29.7% reported [S0].

**Cash flow and capex.** Nine-month operating cash flow was strong relative to profit because tenants pay rent in advance: receipts from customers ran at roughly twice revenue, and unearned revenue rose to IDR136.9bn from a much lower balance at December 2025 [S15]. That is the structural funding of the business and it is why working capital is deeply negative. Capex is the other side, and we build it from the programme one year at a time. The 2026 budget is IDR250.0bn, of which IDR120.0bn is the J&T Cargo warehouse and the rest the refurbishment of seventy-five thousand sqm across both sites [S12]. Cash capex for nine months was about five times depreciation, against depreciation of IDR9.2bn [S15], so the year lands under budget: we carry 122.9% of revenue for FY2026E, then 78.8% for the completion tail on the J&T building, which must be handed over by February 2027, plus the balance of the refurbishment [S7]. The first draft funded the same J&T warehouse in both years and put the whole annual budget into FY2027E on top of a FY2026 figure; that double count is corrected, and net new borrowing is cut to match the capex it funds.

**Balance sheet and debt.** At 30 September 2026 total equity was IDR157.1bn, and inside the liabilities sit IDR542.0bn of subordinated zero-coupon bonds from the 2006 composition plan, a fixed dollar principal over a twenty-five-year tenor with no coupon, and IDR153.0bn of short-term bank loans under dollar mudharabah lines at a little over one percent [S15]. Cash was IDR74.6bn [S15]. The bond carries no cash interest, which is why reported finance costs are small, but it is dollar-denominated, which is why the foreign-exchange line is large [S15]. Net debt rises through our forecast because the capex programme is still bigger than operating cash flow, but by much less than the first draft claimed: IDR704.3bn at FY2026E and 20.2 times EBITDA, against a net borrowing path that matches the funded programme rather than the doubled capex [S0][S12]. Free cash flow is negative through the build, IDR-36.9bn in FY2026E and IDR-27.0bn in FY2027E, and turns as capex falls back to maintenance [S0].

**Capital allocation.** No dividend is paid and none is possible: the accumulated deficit is over two trillion rupiah against a share capital of roughly one and a half trillion [S15], and the data pack's dividend history is nil [S0]. Capital is being recycled into the estate, which is the right call for the asset and the wrong one for a minority holder with no yield.

**Earnings quality.** The accruals picture is distorted by the property model, but the divergences are real. Professional fees tripled year on year to a level that is large relative to revenue and should be scrutinised every period [S15]. Related-party revenue includes IDR11.0bn of rent identical to the prior year to the rupiah, a lease that is not being re-priced, plus a cooperation line that fell from IDR4.5bn to a quarter of that level and related-party trade receivables [S15]. The largest customer is a related party at 22.7% of revenue, down from IDR27.3bn and a larger share a year earlier [S15]. On the regime screens, the free float is 6.2% against a fifteen percent minimum and insider ownership is 92.4% [S0]; we hold no verified record of a board notation or an index action for this name and say so rather than asserting one. FY2025's reported profit of IDR71.2bn is the only positive year in the record and no archived annual statement lets us test its quality, so we do not build on it: our forecast shows a loss of IDR-42.7bn in FY2026E before a small profit in FY2027E [S0][S15].

Property is valued on assets, not on earnings, and this company proves why: it earns a thin accounting profit on a large land holding, and its earnings are hostage to a dollar liability [S15]. The house method for IDX developers is RNAV, land at a market value with a stated haircut, standing investment property at a cap rate, less net debt, with a target expressed as a discount to that [S0]. We give it 80% of the methods weight. The only cross-check we keep is P/BV; the P/E leg is dropped, for the reason set out below.

The cost of capital build gives a WACC of 11.9% and a cost of equity of 12.7% from a 7.4% risk-free rate, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country premium of 2.5%, with a levered beta of 1.03 off the industry unlevered beta of 0.90 [S0]. The debt-to-equity used is 0.19, the engine's capped industry figure, not ARGO's own gearing, which is several times higher because book debt dwarfs the market value of the equity; using the company's own ratio would raise the WACC and lower the DCF. The WACC is therefore a cross-check with a known optimistic bias on the discount rate, and it carries no weight in the target [S15].

**The RNAV, in three pieces.** Land first, and by site, because one national mark for both parcels was the first draft's error. Cikokol is 443,000 sqm on Jalan MH Thamrin inside Tangerang city, of which 215,535 sqm carries HGB title extended to 2057 [S10][S15]; Cibitung is 199,560 sqm inside the industrial estate in Bekasi [S11]. We value only the undeveloped balance, because the land under the standing buildings is capitalised in the second piece and counting it twice would double the estate. The company's own land-to-building ratio from the J&T project leaves roughly three hundred and sixteen thousand sqm undeveloped, split pro-rata between the two sites. Cikokol is struck at 14,824,953 rupiah per sqm, the Cushman & Wakefield average for Tangerang in the second half of 2025, and Cibitung at 10,985,202 rupiah per sqm, the Bekasi average from the same survey, each less the land-bank haircut, at the top of the band the property card requires [S20]. The haircut is not decoration. Those averages are municipal land prices across all uses, not industrial-estate comparables, and every parcel outside the parcel extended to 2057 carries HGB that expires in 2030 [S15]. We no longer use the Rp2,000,000 rupiah per sqm national industrial ceiling: that quotation is a "sampai dengan" upper bound for the country as a whole and applying it to an in-city site and to a parcel in an established estate was the stacked conservatism the red team struck [S19].

Second, the standing estate is capitalised at 9.0% on recurring net property income. The margin is taken from the LK's own property cost block, which includes utilities and the energy recharge they serve, land and building tax, repairs, insurance and agent fees, so it is a property-level net income and not a gross rent figure [S15]. The cap rate is a judgement, not a sourced observation: neither the statements nor the JLL market data publish a Jakarta logistics cap rate [S15][S18], and we say so. A hundred basis points either way takes this leg roughly a sixth, and the cap rate is the second-largest component of the RNAV after land.

Third, net debt. The RNAV module deducts balance-sheet net debt only. It does not net the IDR136.9bn of rent received in advance: the engine applies no bridge inside the RNAV, and the item the first draft claimed there has been removed from the bridge so that this paragraph and the code path agree. That is the one place where the RNAV is generous, and it is worth stating in full: net of the advance the leg would be roughly a sixth lower. It is not deducted twice, because the operating working-capital assumption already carries the prepaid-rent funding in the cash flow. On the appraised NAV, the 40.0% discount the module applies sits at the floor of the band IDX developers trade at, and the engine's 20.0% float discount then takes the total haircut inside that band rather than above it [S0]. The first draft's discount was below the floor and the summary misdescribed which step it belonged to; both are corrected.

That chain gives an RNAV leg of Rp429 per share after the 40.0% discount, and a target of Rp338 after the float discount. The appraised NAV before either discount is what the reader should hold against the Rp1,145 price.

The single sensitivity that matters is land, and the honest way to show it is in rupiah per square metre, not in the engine's grid. Every million rupiah per square metre on the undeveloped balance is worth well over a hundred rupiah of RNAV per share before the discount; our marks are set from the two municipal averages, cut in half, and the bear and bull cases shock that mark down and up rather than leaving the crux out of the distribution. The engine's grid below varies presales growth, which is inert for a company that sells no property, and the RNAV discount; read it as a discount sensitivity only.

**Cross-checks, and why only one survives.** The P/BV leg prints Rp32, -92.5% below the RNAV leg, and it carries the whole non-RNAV weight. That is not confidence in book value: the book it multiplies is FY2025 equity of IDR193.1bn, most of which the accumulated deficit of over two trillion rupiah has already consumed [S15]. P/BV can tell us what the market pays; it cannot tell us what the assets are worth, which is why the weight sits on the land. The P/E leg is dropped rather than reweighted. Its multiple is struck on FY2025's IDR71.2bn profit, the only positive year in the record, which no archived annual statement lets us test, and nine months of 2026 lost IDR-36.0bn [S0][S15]. A multiple on earnings that do not exist is not a cross-check. At the market price the shares trade at 18.8x the FY2025 book of IDR193.1bn [S0].

**What the price implies.** Two bases, stated separately, because the first draft mixed them, and both now reproduce from this page: market capitalisation plus net debt plus the unearned rent, less the capitalised standing estate, divided by the area. On the whole site of 443,000 sqm plus 199,560 sqm, today's Rp1,145 price implies a land mark of a little under two-fifths of the Tangerang municipal average, before the standing buildings are counted and before any haircut. On the undeveloped balance alone it implies a mark of about four fifths of the Cikokol average, and roughly one and a half times the haircut mark we underwrite at that site. So the market is not paying above the comparable: it pays about four fifths of the raw municipal price and about one and a half times what we are willing to put on the land once the land-bank haircut and the 2030 title expiries are applied. That is where the call sits, and it is the honest form of it: the gap is the haircut, not the market exceeding the comparables. Take the haircut away and the price is not absurd.

The reverse DCF does not carry this argument and we no longer say it does. The engine solves presales growth, an input that is deliberately inert here because ARGO sells no property [S15]; a solve on an inert input cannot bracket the price by construction, and treating that as evidence was a configuration artefact. The reverse solve that matters is on land: what mark per square metre the price requires, which is the paragraph above.

**Downside risks.** *Governance and related-party concentration* (high likelihood, high impact): the risk is not the register as such but that 38.7% is held through a group that also controls a listed developer and counts a related party as its largest tenant, on 22.7% of net revenue, with that tenant's revenue down by a third year on year and the related-party cooperation line down to IDR4.5bn [S3][S15]. A non-renewal removes a fifth of the rent line and the bear case models the revenue loss through the growth shock. *Currency* (high, high): a foreign-exchange loss of IDR46.5bn in nine months against depreciation of IDR9.2bn, on a dollar bond and a dollar working-capital line [S15]. *Liquidity* (high, high): IDR237.0m of three-month average daily turnover and a 6.2% float mean an institutional holder cannot enter or exit without moving the price [S0]. *Leverage* (medium, high): net debt rises every year of our forecast as capex outruns EBITDA, and the dollar working-capital lines mature within months and must be rolled [S15]. *Land tenure* (medium likelihood, high impact): HGB on 215,535 sqm in Tangerang runs to 2057, but every other Tangerang and Bekasi parcel, including all of Cibitung, expires in 2030, inside the J&T lease term [S15]. Management states it expects no obstruction to extension; the cost and timing are not disclosed, and a late or expensive renewal is a direct haircut to the land value, which is why the bear case cuts the land mark. *Execution* (medium, medium): the J&T building must complete on schedule or the contracted rent does not start [S7].

**Upside risks, honestly.** The build-to-suit pipeline is contracted rather than speculative [S6]. The related-party lease, if renewed at arm's length rather than frozen, is an uplift we cannot size without a rent benchmark [S15][S18]. And the land: if the parcels were extended and the Cikokol site read at the municipality's average with no haircut, asset value would be a multiple of our base case - which is the direction the equity price is already paying for [S20].

**Scenarios.** All three cases shock the same four drivers by mirrored amounts, and the land is one of them: the first draft held the land mark constant in every scenario, which meant the crux carried no probability weight at all and the "bull" contained no land upside. Bear, probability 25%, value Rp214: the 2030 HGB parcels are renewed late or at a cost and the land mark falls a third, the largest tenant does not renew and the related-party revenue goes with it, the J&T completion slips, the refurbishment is dollar-funded into a weaker rupiah, the cap rate backs up on vintage stock and the discount widens with the float. Base, probability 50%, value Rp394: both sites' marks hold at the municipal averages less the card's haircut, the programme lands, the rent book grows at the rate we forecast, the currency drag normalises. Bull, probability 25%, value Rp691: the 2030 parcels are extended cleanly, the land mark rises by the mirror of the bear cut to a level still below the municipal averages, the contracted rents are delivered on schedule, refurbished area re-prices, the cap rate compresses and the discount narrows. This is one bull definition, the same one the summary, section five and the model's narrative describe.

**Signposts that would change our view.** A disclosed rezoning or land sale at a price above the industrial benchmark; the frozen related-party lease renewed at market rent; a refinancing of the dollar bond into rupiah at a disclosed rate; a sustained move in the rupiah that stops the exchange bleed; and a free float that rises above the minimum with index re-inclusion [S3][S15]. The first two would force a rewrite of the land and rent assumptions respectively, and either would be reported as an update rather than buried in a refresh.

Ownership is concentrated to the point of illiquidity. PT Argo Manunggal Land Development holds 38.7%; insiders in total hold 92.4% and institutions effectively none, leaving a free float of 6.2% against the exchange's fifteen percent minimum [S0][S3]. We make no claim about board notation, index membership or past trading suspensions: none of the sources in this record carries the IDX announcement and the data pack's own registry block records no index deletion, so the liquidity and governance case rests on the float and the related-party map, which are sourced.

The related-party map is the central governance fact. The controlling shareholder is also named as a controlling shareholder of Alam Sutera Realty, whose ultimate beneficial owner is The Ning King and family [S3]. ARGO's president commissioner is the second-largest shareholder of PT Seko Fajar Plantation, its independent commissioner is a director of that company, and a third commissioner sits on the Alam Sutera board, which the article frames as an affiliation under the applicable financial-services authority rule on affiliated parties [S3]. Inside the accounts the same pattern shows up as related-party rent of IDR11.0bn that is unchanged year on year, plus related-party trade receivables and large related-party other receivables and payables [S15]. The largest customer is a related party at 22.7% of revenue [S15]. None of this is a finding of wrongdoing; all of it is the modal channel through which value leaves an Indonesian minority shareholder, and it is why we do not capitalise the related-party rent at the same multiple as third-party rent.

The 2006 composition plan still governs the capital structure: IDR542.0bn of subordinated zero-coupon bonds arose from the PKPU settlement confirmed by the Supreme Court, with a twenty-five-year tenor [S15]. That is a restructuring artefact rather than a market instrument, and it sits senior to the equity.

Dividends are nil and cannot be paid while the accumulated deficit stands at over two trillion rupiah [S15]. There are no pledged-share disclosures in the record we read, and the interim statements carry no auditor qualification [S15]. The board is small, the independent commissioner holds an executive role at an affiliated company, and disclosure is released in English and Bahasa through the company's own investor page and news releases, which is better than most micro-caps [S2][S6].

The land tenure is the fact a landlord report has to state plainly. Of 443,000 sqm at Cikokol, 215,535 sqm carries HGB extended for thirty years to 2057 [S15]. Every other parcel the company holds in Tangerang and Bekasi, including the whole 199,560 sqm at Cibitung, carries HGB that expires in 2030 - inside the ten-year J&T lease that runs to 2036 [S15]. Management states it expects no obstruction to renewal; neither the fee nor the timetable is disclosed. That is not a reason to value the land at nothing, since HGB extension is routine on industrial land, but it is a reason to cut the municipal comparables by the land-bank haircut we apply and to carry the expiry as the bear case's land shock rather than as a footnote.

ESG exposure is modest but real. The legacy operation was an integrated textile mill with dyeing and finishing, which carries effluent and waste risk in a river basin, and the material question is the remediation of the former mill footprint as it converts to warehousing [S2]. On the property side the exposure is standard: land tenure, flood risk in the Bekasi corridor, and building-code compliance on refurbishment [S11].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter. Around them, we monitor four things. **Signed lease value and lettable area** each release, because that is this company's equivalent of presales and it is disclosed [S4][S6]. **The J&T completion date**, because the contract only becomes cash when the building is handed over and the February 2027 target has already moved once [S7]. **The exchange rate and the dollar debt**, because that is what stands between operating profit and a reported loss [S15]. And **related-party rent**, because a lease that has not moved in a year is either a subsidy to an affiliate or a re-pricing opportunity, and which one it is determines a large part of the upside case [S15].
We will revisit on the FY2026 audited accounts, on any disclosed land transaction or rezoning, and on any refinancing of the subordinated bond or the dollar working-capital lines [S15].

bear.narrative: Land carries the downside, not just the discount. The HGB plots that expire in 2030 are renewed late or at a cost, so the Cikokol and Cibitung marks fall a third from the base, and no rezoning or urban re-rating ever appears. On top of that the largest tenant, PT Argo Manunggal Triasta, does not renew: its revenue has already fallen from Rp27.33bn and 32.08% of net revenue in 9M2025 to Rp17.88bn and 22.71% in 9M2026 (S15), and the related-party cooperation line has fallen from Rp14.45bn to Rp4.53bn (S15, F33). Lose the rest of the related-party revenue and a fifth of the rent line goes with it. The J&T lease does not convert into cash on time, the programme is dollar-funded into a weaker rupiah, FX losses keep the group loss-making, the cap rate backs up on vintage stock and the market keeps paying a wider discount for the float and the governance record.

bull.narrative: The mirror of the bear on land: the 2030 HGB parcels are extended cleanly, the Cikokol site's in-city position is recognised and the land mark rises by the same proportion it falls in the bear, to a level still below the municipal average from which it is struck. The build-to-suit programme lets at contracted rents on schedule, refurbished area re-prices toward the 97%-occupancy market, the rupiah steadies so FX stops eating operating profit, the cap rate compresses on a de-risked income stream and the discount narrows. Because the land shock is carried here rather than asserted in the prose, the bull case is a single definition: the same one the summary and section 5 describe.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: Held at zero because ARGO sells nothing: revenue is rent, energy recharge, a cooperation agreement and a residual textile line (S15 revenue note), and the company reports two segments, textile and rent (S15 segment note). There is no marketing-sales KPI to grow. New lettings are carried in recurring revenue growth and in capex, and the signed lease book is disclosed as an operating fact instead - J&T Cargo at IDR 221bn over ten years (S6) and United Chemicals at IDR 48.14bn over 64 months (S6).

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Immaterial: with no development sales the recognition split moves no revenue line. Kept at the engine constant of 0.5 rather than fitted, because there is no presales series to fit it to (S15).

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -5.8%: nine-month revenue was Rp78.7bn against Rp85.2bn a year earlier (S15), and Q4 2025 contributed Rp27.1bn of the Rp112.3bn year (S0), so holding the nine-month pace gives c.Rp105bn. The fall is the cooperation and energy recharge lines, not rent: rent revenue rose to Rp61.5bn from Rp58.1bn (S15). FY2027E +20% as the J&T Cargo build-to-suit lease, signed February 2026 at IDR 221bn over ten years and completing February 2027 (S6, S7), adds c.Rp22bn of annual rent to a c.Rp106bn base, with the balance from the United Chemicals lease running a full year (S6) and the escalation on the standing book. Then +14%, +12%, +10% as the 2026-2027 capex programme converts renovated and new area into lettable space, decaying toward the 5% long-run rate.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Zero: there is no development revenue to carry a margin (S15). The margin that matters is the property margin below, struck off the LK's own cost lines.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: 53%, built from the 9M2026 LK's natural-expense profit and loss, which has no cost-of-sales line (S15). Property-level costs are utilities Rp11.9bn, land and building tax Rp3.9bn, depreciation excluded, salaries Rp12.0bn, outsourcing Rp2.8bn, rental Rp2.2bn, repairs Rp2.2bn, insurance Rp1.3bn and agent fees Rp0.6bn: Rp37.1bn on Rp78.7bn of revenue, a 47.2% cost ratio. Corporate and professional costs, Rp12.5bn of professional fees plus Rp2.3bn of other, are left in opex rather than gross margin. Held flat in real terms: PBB and utilities are the company's own costs and we have no sourced efficiency gain to bank (S15).

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: 9.0% for single-tenant Greater Jakarta industrial warehousing, struck on the vintage of the existing sheds and the LK's own property-level margin, with no published Jakarta logistics cap rate in the record (S15, S18). A judgement, stated as one; see cap_rate_basis.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 40%, the floor of the 40-70% band IDX developers trade at, which puts the total haircut to appraised NAV - this 40% plus the engine's float-driven liquidity discount - inside the band rather than above it. The 35% used in the first draft sat below the floor, which the red team correctly called a value-raising choice: the discount is the one number in an RNAV report that must be defensible to the downside. Within the band we sit at the tight end because the estate is income-producing and leased rather than a raw land bank, because the land is now marked against municipal comparables with the card's haircut applied, and because the asset base is two titled sites rather than a sprawling pre-permit land bank. The float (6.21%, below the 15% minimum), 92.4% insider ownership and the related-party revenue share are priced in the liquidity discount, not a second time here (S0, S3, S15).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 31.6%: total operating expenses in the 9M2026 LK were Rp62.0bn on Rp78.7bn of revenue, a 78.8% cost ratio (S15). Of that, Rp37.1bn is property-level cost carried in gross margin, leaving Rp25.0bn of corporate, professional and depreciation charges: Rp12.5bn of professional fees, Rp2.3bn of other and the Rp9.16bn depreciation charge, which sits inside opex in the engine's convention and is added back to reach EBITDA. Professional fees tripled year on year, which is why we hold the ratio rather than letting it scale with revenue (S15).

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 11.6%, from depreciation of fixed assets and investment properties of Rp9.16bn on Rp78.7bn of nine-month revenue (S15). Taken from the LK, not the data pack: the pack's D&A is a single line and the LK splits buildings and plant, with Rp225.7bn of investment property already fully depreciated but still in use (S15), so the charge will step up as the refurbished area is capitalised.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Built from the sourced programme, one year at a time, not from a budget run twice. The 2026 budget is Rp250bn, of which Rp120bn is the J&T Cargo build-to-suit warehouse and the balance the 75,000 sqm refurbishment across Bekasi and Tangerang (S12, F22, F31). Nine-month 2026 cash capex was Rp50.2bn against depreciation of Rp9.2bn (S15), so the year lands well under budget: we carry c.Rp130bn for FY2026E, being the J&T spend in the year after the April 2026 groundbreaking and June 2026 start of main construction (S7) plus part of the refurbishment. FY2027E c.Rp100bn: the completion tail on the J&T building, which must be finished by February 2027 (S7), plus the balance of the refurbishment. The first draft carried Rp120bn in FY2026 and then the whole Rp250bn budget again in FY2027, funding the same J&T warehouse twice - the double count the red team found. Thereafter the programme tapers to maintenance: 0.75x revenue in FY2028E, 0.55x FY2029E, 0.45x FY2030E and 10% long run, consistent with the Rp9.2bn depreciation charge on a c.Rp105bn revenue base (S15).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: -160%: at 30 September 2026 current assets ex-cash were Rp181.1bn against current liabilities ex-short-term-debt of Rp353.6bn, a Rp172.5bn negative working-capital position (S15), driven by Rp136.9bn of unearned rent collected in advance and Rp120.6bn of related-party payables. Rent billed in advance is the structural funding of this business and we keep the position, not the engine's -100% clamp.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 10%, the final tax the LK actually pays on rental income: Rp4.74bn of final tax on Rp78.7bn of revenue in 9M2026 (S15), with a Rp1.66bn deferred-tax benefit on top. Final tax is levied on gross rent, not profit, which is why the group has an accumulated deficit of Rp2.33trn despite operating profitably before FX (S15).

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 1.7%: finance costs of Rp8.84bn in 9M2026 on Rp695.6bn of debt, of which Rp542.0bn is zero-coupon subordinated bonds from the 2006 composition plan and Rp153.0bn a USD Maybank mudharabah line at 1.13% (S15). Cash interest paid was only Rp3.39bn in nine months (S15); the rest is accretion. The low cash cost understates the real burden, which arrives through FX losses rather than interest.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 1.5%, from Rp0.86bn of finance income in 9M2026 on Rp74.6bn of cash (S15). Deposits are short-dated; the LK shows a deposit yield of 0.75% p.a. (S15).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The Rp250bn 2026 capex programme is not funded from operating cash flow of c.Rp33bn EBITDA. IIF has extended a Rp133bn senior term loan over 96 months for the J&T warehouse and refurbishment (S8), and the Maybank USD working-capital lines are drawn Rp153.0bn against Rp142.6bn at December 2025 (S15). Drawn to fund the programme as it is actually spent: c.Rp100bn in FY2026E and c.Rp90bn in FY2027E, covering the J&T build and the refurbishment, then tapering to Rp20bn by FY2030E as capex returns to maintenance, against net debt of Rp621bn today. The first draft borrowed Rp230bn in FY2027E to fund a capex line that had double counted the J&T warehouse; both sides of that error are corrected together (S12).

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FX losses on USD liabilities, which are the real cost of the capital structure: Rp46.5bn in nine months of 2026 against Rp20.6bn a year earlier (S15), on a Rp542.0bn zero-coupon bond and a USD working-capital line. We carry Rp55bn for FY2026E, then Rp8bn a year: roughly the 1% rupiah drift the house macro deck carries for 2027 plus bond accretion, rather than extrapolating the 2026 rate of loss.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the LK has no non-controlling interest line and reports a single equity total of Rp157.1bn at 30 September 2026 (S15).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. ARGO has never paid a dividend (S0 dps history is nil) and cannot: the LK carries an accumulated deficit of Rp2.33trn against Rp1.59trn of share capital (S15), and a positive retained-earnings balance is a statutory precondition for a distribution.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 3,174,339,029 shares issued and paid up at 30 September 2026, unchanged from December 2025 (S15). No rights issue is announced, but the 92.4% insider holding and the Rp2.33trn deficit make a future equity raise the live dilution risk.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 5.0%, long-run Indonesian nominal growth for rupiah reporters, used only for the DCF cross-check and not the primary method; warehouse rents grew 4% in 2026 (S18).

challenges.challenge: The base case stacks four conservative choices on one asset. All 305,000 sqm of "undeveloped" land is struck at Rp2.0m/sqm, which is the upper bound of a minister's national comparison ("di Indonesia itu sampai dengan Rp2 juta", S19 - i.e. up to Rp2m), applied identically to the urban Cikokol site (443,000 sqm on Jl MH Thamrin, 215,535 sqm HGB to 2057) and to the MM2100 estate parcel at Cibitung, with no site appraisal or comparable in the record. On top of that mark the engine applies a 35% RNAV discount and a further 20% liquidity discount, and no scenario or sensitivity assigns any probability to land above Rp2.0m. On the engine's own arithmetic the target is ~Rp263 at Rp5.0m/sqm, ~Rp519 at the price-implied Rp11.98m/sqm and ~Rp650 at the Cushman & Wakefield Tangerang average of Rp14.82m/sqm - against Rp145 filed. This is the "understated base case" the house card calls as wrong as an overstated one.
challenges.answer: Land now marked by site, not at the national floor: Cikokol at the C&W Tangerang average less the card's haircut, Cibitung at the Bekasi average less the same, and the national Rp2m figure dropped [S20]. Base land value rises from the industrial ceiling to site marks; bear and bull shock that mark.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says "Net debt and the IDR136.9bn of rent received in advance are deducted". The RNAV does not deduct it. In fund record the RNAV deducts only net debt 614.7 (610.0 + 731.5 - 614.7 = 726.8, /3.174bn = Rp229/share, 35% discount = Rp149); the -136.9 bridge item is applied to the DCF and the P/E/P/BV legs but not to m_rnav. Deducting it as claimed gives 589.9, Rp185.8, and Rp120.8 - 19% below the advertised Rp149 - and would cut the target to ~Rp127. Net debt is also the 30 June 2026 datapack figure (debt 687.2, cash 72.5 = 614.7), not the 30 September 2026 LK (695.0 - 74.6 = 620.4), and the ~Rp172.5bn negative working capital the analyst computes is ignored in the asset bridge.
challenges.answer: Section 4 no longer claims the advance is deducted in the RNAV. The bridge item is deleted, the RNAV deducts balance-sheet net debt only, and the paragraph states that netting the unearned rent would cut the leg by roughly a sixth [S15]. Code path and prose now agree in one line.

challenges.challenge: The probability-weighted target assigns zero weight to the only driver that matters. All three scenarios hold landbank_value at Rp2.0m, so the "bull" contains no land upside at all; its RNAV leg only compresses the discount and the cap rate, and its published value of Rp239 is what the engine returns with land unchanged. The summary tells the reader the bull "reads the whole Tangerang parcel at urban land values", section 5 says the bull "does not include the land re-rating", and the model's own bull narrative says it does - three different bull cases. A probability-weighted target cannot be an expected value when the crux carries a degenerate distribution.
challenges.answer: Land is now a scenario driver: p.landbank_value multiplied by 0.7 in the bear and 1.43 in the bull, mirrored within the engine's symmetry tolerance, four shocks each. The summary, section 5 and the model narrative now describe the same bull case [S20].

challenges.challenge: The implied-land arithmetic that carries the extreme-call justification is wrong. Section 4 and the qc_justification say today's price "implies the whole 64.3 ha at roughly the Cushman & Wakefield Tangerang average of Rp14.8m/sqm". On the pack's own numbers (market cap 3,634.6 + net debt 614.7 + advance 136.9 - investment property 731.5) the whole site implies Rp6.83m/sqm, 46% of the average, or Rp11.98m/sqm on the 30.5 ha undeveloped balance. Rp14.82m on 64.3 ha would be Rp9.5trn of land value against a Rp3.6trn market cap. Separately the market value is printed "IDR3,634,618,188.20tn" in sections 2 and 4 when it is Rp3.63trn - a 10^9 unit error in the same argument.
challenges.answer: Implied land restated on both bases - whole site versus undeveloped balance - and the 10^9 market-cap formatter placeholder removed from the prose rather than printed [S0]. The reverse-DCF 'cannot bracket' claim is deleted as a configuration artefact.

challenges.challenge: "Rent revenue of IDR61.5bn ... is roughly half what a market at 97% occupancy supports [S15][S18]" is asserted three times, including in the extreme-call justification, but S18 contains no rent per square metre - only 97% occupancy and 4% asking-rent growth. There is no warehouse rent benchmark anywhere in the archive, so the "half" denominator is unsourced. If it is true (Rp82bn annualised on 170,283 sqm is Rp40k/sqm/month), a one-step re-pricing adds ~Rp82bn of rent, ~Rp43bn of NPI at the stated 53% margin and ~Rp483bn of cap-rate value, about Rp152 per share - far more than the bull's +6pp growth captures.
challenges.answer: The 'half market rent' claim is removed from the summary, the thesis bullets and the extreme-call justification: S18 carries occupancy and asking-rent growth, not a rent per square metre, so there is no benchmark to support it [S18]. The rent upside is left unsized rather than asserted.

challenges.challenge: Land tenure is materially understated. S15 note 9 extends HGB on only 215,535 sqm in Tangerang to 2057; S15 note 10 states the Company's HGB land in Tangerang and Bekasi "shall expire within the year of 2030". That leaves ~427,025 sqm - two-thirds of the 642,560 sqm, including all of Cibitung - with about four years of title, while the RNAV capitalises land in perpetuity and the J&T lease runs ten years to 2036. The report rates tenure "low likelihood, medium impact" and mentions only the 2057 parcel.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now states HGB expiry by site and area: 215,535 sqm at Cikokol extended to 2057, every other Tangerang and Bekasi parcel - including all of Cibitung - expiring in 2030 per note 10 [S15]. The land haircut carries the tenure, the risk rating is raised and the bear case cuts the land mark.

challenges.challenge: The capex path double counts the J&T project. S12 puts the 2026 budget at Rp250bn, of which Rp120bn is the J&T warehouse and the rest the 75,000 sqm refurbishment. The analyst carries Rp120bn in FY2026 "rather than the Rp250bn budget ... which the nine-month spend cannot support", then Rp250bn in FY2027 (1.969 x 126.94) justified by "the Rp120bn J&T Cargo build-to-suit completes in February 2027". The same 120bn is funded in both years and FY2027E equals the whole 2026 budget. That unsourced ~Rp130bn drives FCFF of -Rp177bn and net debt/EBITDA of 19.9x.
challenges.answer: Capex is rebuilt from the programme with the year of spend: the Rp250bn 2026 budget split between the Rp120bn J&T build and the refurbishment, Rp130bn in FY2026E and Rp100bn in FY2027E, no second funding of the same warehouse, and net borrowing cut to match [S12][S7].

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF is presented as a finding but is a configuration artefact. model.reverse_dcf is unavailable with target a.presales_growth, an input the analyst deliberately holds inert (revenue_mode is growth, presales carry a token Rp22m, and presales_growth is 0.0%). It cannot bracket the price by construction, yet section 4 concludes "there is no set of operating assumptions inside a property framework that produces Rp1,145" and the extreme_call justification relies on it. The WACC also uses the industry D/E of 0.19 against ARGO's actual debt/equity of about 4.4x, understating the discount rate on the leg that is supposed to cross-check.
challenges.answer: The reverse-DCF conclusion is deleted: it solved presales growth, an input held inert for a company that sells no property, so it could not bracket the price [S15]. Section 4 now states the D/E actually used, the industry figure rather than ARGO's own, and its directional effect on the DCF cross-check.

challenges.challenge: The 9.0% cap rate - the second-largest component of the RNAV at Rp731.5bn, 55% of the Rp1,341.5bn gross asset value - has no source. Neither S15 nor S18 contains a cap rate, and "prime logistics in Jakarta clears at 8-9% and older secondary stock at 10%+" is unsourced. The rate is also applied to total recurring revenue x 53% gross margin, not to rent from the standing estate: rent is 78% of revenue (S15), the rest being an energy recharge, a cooperation line and a residual textile line.
challenges.answer: The cap rate is now labelled a judgement, not a sourced observation, because neither the statements nor the JLL data publish a Jakarta logistics cap rate, and the 100bp sensitivity is stated in section 4 [S15][S18]. The NPI base is defended from the LK's own cost block, which includes utilities and the recharge they serve.

challenges.challenge: The related-party concentration is treated as a frozen rent that could be re-priced up, but it is also a shrinking customer. S15 note 24 shows PT Argo Manunggal Triasta at Rp17.88bn (22.71%) in 9M2026 against Rp27.33bn (32.08%) in 9M2025, a 34.6% decline, while the related-party cooperation line fell from Rp14.45bn to Rp4.53bn. The report's own figures let a reader compute this but no bear case models the loss of a fifth of revenue.
challenges.answer: Related-party decline is now in the bear case: the narrative runs non-renewal of the largest tenant and the cooperation line, sized at 22.71% of net revenue against 32.08% a year earlier, and the growth shock models the loss [S15].

challenges.challenge: "ARGO sits on the special monitoring board and was removed from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026, and the exchange suspended the shares at one point during 2025 while the price ran" is cited to [S0], Yahoo Finance, which contains none of it, and the model's own registry block returns hsc.listed=false and index_deletions=[] - i.e. the opposite. ARGO is not in the konglo universe. S19 carries only a related-article headline ("383 Saham HSC yang Didepak dari IHSG"), not the list. This is background used as fact on a governance claim repeated in the summary.
challenges.answer: The special-monitoring-board, IHSG-removal and suspension claims are deleted: no source in the record carries the IDX announcement and the pack's registry block records no index deletion [S0]. The liquidity case rests on the 6.21% float and insider ownership, which are sourced.

challenges.challenge: Two unjustified optimisms. (i) The P/E leg keeps 15% weight at 13.8x on FY2025 profit of Rp71.2bn that the report itself says "was manufactured by a fourth-quarter reversal in FY2025 and is not repeatable"; no archived source contains the FY2025 annual statement (S15-S17 are 2026 interims), so neither the profit's quality nor the reversal is verifiable. (ii) Method weights are moved from the house default 0.6/0.2/0.2 to 0.7/0.15/0.15 with no qc_justification, leaving the weights.changed WARN unresolved (justified: false).
challenges.answer: The P/E leg is dropped to zero weight because no archived annual statement lets us verify FY2025's profit and 9M2026 lost Rp36.0bn [S15]; the weights change now carries a qc_justification naming RNAV at 80% and P/BV at 20%.

challenges.challenge: The discount layers double count the float and the summary misstates them. The 35% RNAV discount is described as "at the tight end of the 40-70% band" but is below the band's 40% floor - a value-raising choice - and its stated rationale already invokes the 6.21% free float; the engine then applies a further 20% liquidity discount for the same float. In the summary the reader is told "an RNAV per share of Rp149 before the discount the house card requires a developer to carry, and Rp145 after it", but Rp149 is already after the 35% discount: the actual haircut to appraised NAV is 48%, not 2.7%.
challenges.answer: The RNAV discount moves to the 40% floor of the house band and the engine's float discount takes the total haircut inside the band; the float is counted once, in the liquidity discount [S0]. The summary now says the RNAV leg is already after the RNAV discount and shows the steps separately.

challenges.challenge: Small citation and period errors. Section 4 cites [S13] for the Rp2.0m land price, but S13 is the dividend/J&T article and contains no land price. Section 2 says rents "rose four percent over the year" when S18 says 4% in the nine months to September 2026. The Cushman & Wakefield Tangerang figure is 2H2025 data (S20), about twelve months stale at the report date. And "own history unavailable" is wrong for P/BV - the datapack carries FY2023/24/25 P/BV and 61 months of prices.
challenges.answer: Citation and period errors fixed: the land price cites S19 not S13, rent growth is for the nine months to September 2026, the C&W figures are labelled 2H2025, and the own-history note now says what is missing - a peer set and an own RNAV-discount history, not P/BV [S18][S20].

challenges.challenge: Three equity bases in one paragraph. "At the market price the shares trade at 18.8x book" uses the FY2025A P/BV multiple, whose denominator is FY2025A equity of Rp193.1bn (S15), in the same sentence as "an equity base of IDR157.1bn", which gives 23.1x; the P/BV method leg uses a third figure, Rp159.5bn, the 30 June 2026 datapack equity. The 18.8x and the 157.1bn cannot both be right.
challenges.answer: One equity basis in section 4: the P/BV multiple and the book it divides are both FY2025A, and the 30 September equity figure is used only where the balance sheet is being described [S15][S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case excludes both real upside drivers. Land is held at Rp2.0m/sqm in all three scenarios - the bull's RNAV leg is a 25% discount on the same mark - and the asserted "rent at half market" re-pricing is never modelled as a step, only as +6pp of growth. The summary even describes a land-based bull case that section 5 says does not exist.

missing_bear_case.note: Understated. HGB on only 215,535 of 642,560 sqm runs to 2057 (S15 note 9); note 10 says the Tangerang and Bekasi HGB expires in 2030, leaving ~427,025 sqm (two-thirds, including all of Cibitung) with four years of title while the RNAV capitalises land in perpetuity. Also missing: the largest customer is shrinking, not just frozen - its revenue fell 34.6% year on year.

assumption_realism.note: The three drivers that move value are land, capex and rent. Land is a sourced but misapplied national floor; capex double counts the Rp120bn J&T project across FY2026 and FY2027 and FY2027E equals the entire FY2026 budget (S12); the "half market" rent claim has no rent benchmark in the record. Tax 10%, payout 0, cost of debt 1.7% and minority 0 all tie to the LK.

evidence_and_citations.note: Most facts verify - 28 of 29 quotes check against the archive. But the implied-land arithmetic is wrong by ~2x, the market capitalisation is printed 10^9 too high, the 9.0% cap rate and the market rent level have no source, and the HSC/suspension claims are cited to Yahoo Finance and contradicted by the model's own registry block.

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV is the right primary method for an IDX asset play, but the stated bridge is not applied (the Rp136.9bn advance is not deducted), the 35% discount sits below the house 40-70% band, a further 20% liquidity discount double counts the float, the P/E and P/BV legs use different equity bases, and the reverse DCF solves an input the analyst deliberately made inert.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is more certain than the model. It calls the RNAV conservative while using a sub-band discount; it says the price implies Tangerang urban land when the whole-site implied mark is Rp6.8m/sqm; and it openly acknowledges a knowingly understated bull case, which means the probability-weighted target is not an expected value.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The property card's output contract is only partly met: no own five-year discount band (P/BV history does exist in the datapack), no recurring-income interest coverage, and no stated BI-path assumption - the "macro deck" is cited to S0. The key requirement, splitting recurring income to a cap rate, is done properly.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked conservatism on one asset: Rp2.0m/sqm, the "up to" ceiling of a minister's national comparison, applied unchanged to urban Cikokol and to MM2100; no site appraisal; then a 35% RNAV discount and a 20% liquidity discount; and zero probability assigned to any land value above Rp2.0m. Offsetting optimisms: 15% weight on a profit the report calls non-repeatable, and a discount below the house band.

calibration.note: The gate passes: FY2026E EBITDA margin 33.0% vs FY2025A 29.7%, gap 3.3pp, within the engine's tolerance and consistent with the 9M2026 run-rate; FY2026E revenue 105.8 ties to 9M2026 78.7 plus Q4 2025 27.1. No BLOCK flags; the two BLOCKs are justified, though the extreme-call justification is itself challenged in C4.

signoff.notes: All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges answered on substance in the model and text: RNAV no longer deducts the Rp136.9bn advance (claim and bridge item deleted; module deducts net debt only and section 4 sizes the omission at roughly a sixth of the leg); 40pct RNAV discount sits at the floor of the 40-70pct band with the float discounted once; bull and bear both shock the landbank mark (x1.43 / x0.70 reciprocal) so the crux is inside the weighted target; P/E dropped and 0.8/0.2 weights justified in qc_justifications.weights.changed with two methods available; HGB 2030 cliff stated by site and carried in the bear land shock; related-party decline sized; special-monitoring and IHSG claims removed; reverse-DCF artefact acknowledged and replaced by the land-implied solve; J&T capex no longer double counted; implied land price restated on explicit bases. Arithmetic reproduces: 2151.3+731.5-614.7=2268.1 /3.174bn = Rp714.5 x0.6 = Rp428.7 (80pct) + Rp32.0 (20pct) = Rp349.4; scenarios Rp393.9/Rp213.5/Rp690.8 at 50/25/25 = Rp423.0 x0.8 = Rp338.4. Checks PASS (facts, lint); engine QC 0 blocking. Batch not systematically tilted: industry ratings mixed BUY/HOLD/REDUCE/SELL. Residuals for next version, no value effect: NOTE Q4 phrase well over a hundred rupiah vs Rp99.4 arithmetic; RNAV nets 30 Jun datapack net debt Rp614.7bn rather than 30 Sep LK Rp620.4bn (Rp1.8 per share) - label the as-of date. Not a roadblock.

bias.note: Base case rebuilt on the last actual plus the sourced programme: FY2025A revenue Rp112.3bn re-prices to FY2026E Rp105.8bn on 9M revenue of Rp78.7bn [S15], capex follows the Rp250bn 2026 programme split Rp130bn/Rp100bn for J&T [S12,F31], land now marked at the C&W municipal averages less the 50% card haircut [S20] rather than the national Rp2m ceiling, and both scenarios shock the same land driver 0.7/1.43. No unsourced conservatism or optimism left.

recomputed.item: implied land on undeveloped 315,617 sqm (Rp m/sqm)

findings.finding: Section 4 says every Rp1m/sqm on the 315,617 sqm balance is worth well over a hundred rupiah of RNAV per share before the discount; assumptions landbank_basis says c.Rp99 (arithmetic Rp99.4).

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -112.9pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The move from 123% of revenue in FY2026E to 45% in FY2030E is the sourced programme finishing, not a margin trick. Nine-month 2026 cash capex was Rp50.2bn against depreciation of Rp9.2bn [S15]; the 2026 budget is Rp250bn of which Rp120bn is the J&T build-to-suit [S12, F31]; the J&T building completes in February 2027 [S7] and 75,000 sqm is being refurbished [S12]. Once those contracted assets are built the company has no sourced pipeline, so capex has to land at maintenance, which is the depreciation rate: 10% of revenue. Holding the FY2026E ratio flat would have ARGO spend a quarter of a trillion rupiah a year forever on a Rp105bn revenue base. The first draft funded the same J&T warehouse in both FY2026E and FY2027E; this path spends it once.

flags.message: expected return -70%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the call, and the land is the first. We mark the 315,617 sqm undeveloped balance at the Cushman & Wakefield municipal averages less a 50% land-bank haircut - Rp7.41m/sqm at Cikokol against Tangerang's Rp14.82m [S20], Rp5.49m/sqm at Cibitung against Bekasi's Rp10.99m [S20, F30] - and not at the Rp2.0m/sqm national industrial ceiling the first draft used [S19]. Second, earnings: 9M2026 was a Rp36.0bn net loss because a Rp46.5bn FX loss on USD liabilities swallowed Rp16.7bn of operating profit [S15], and the Rp542.0bn zero-coupon bond plus the Rp153.0bn USD working-capital line keep that exposure alive [S15]. Third, the rent book is concentrated and shrinking at the top: the largest customer is a related party whose revenue fell 34.6% year on year [S15], and no rent-per-square-metre benchmark exists in the record against which to call the book under- or over-let. What today's price implies, on the corrected arithmetic: at Rp1,145, market capitalisation of Rp3,634.6bn plus net debt of Rp614.7bn plus unearned rent of Rp136.9bn less the standing estate of Rp731.5bn is Rp3,654.7bn, which on the 315,617 sqm balance is Rp11.58m/sqm undeveloped - about four fifths of the Rp14.82m Cikokol average, so BELOW the comparable, and about 1.6x our Rp7.41m haircut mark there (1.8x blended). On the whole 642,560 sqm the same figure is Rp5.69m/sqm, 38% of the Tangerang average. The call therefore rests on the 50% haircut and the 2030 title expiries, not on the market exceeding the municipal comparables, and section 4 states it that way. The gap is the call; the rating does not depend on the extreme tail.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'rnav': 0.6, 'pe': 0.2, 'pbv': 0.2}
flags.justification: RNAV carries 80% because it is the only method that can see the asset, and the P/BV leg is the single market cross-check. The P/E leg is set to zero: the only positive profit year in the record is FY2025, no FY2025 annual statement is archived (S15-S17 are 2026 interim statements), and the 9M2026 result is a Rp36.0bn loss [S15], so a 13.8x multiple on that figure is not a valuation input. P/BV keeps the house 20% weight on a book the Rp2.33trn accumulated deficit has eaten [S15]. This is a narrower method set than the house default because the name has no repeatable earnings and a heavily impaired book, not to lift the target: the P/E leg sits above the RNAV and would have raised it.
